mainTopic: Why an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is כשר but not מרצה, and whether offerings brought after death atone for the heirs
overview: The גמרא looks for a source that an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is still כשר but does not count for its owner. Proofs from תודה, and then a הצד השוה built from תודה, עולה and שלמים, are both knocked down. רבא finally brings a הקש from the פסוק 'זאת התורה', which places אשם next to שלמים. The word 'אותה' keeps the strict חטאת law from spreading to other offerings. Next, רב הונא, רב נחמן and רב ששת discuss ריש לקיש's difficulty. They explain that the word 'הוא' makes only a חטאת פסול שלא לשמה. For אשם, the same word teaches that it stays an אשם until it is ניתק לרעיה. A second group asks whether offerings brought after the owner's death could atone for the heirs. That question leads to a back-and-forth, which continues on the next amud, about whether the heirs own an inherited offering.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof from a thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: The attempt to learn אשם from תודה fails, because a תודה is special: it needs bread brought with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a תודה? It is different, because it requires bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the attempt to learn the law of אשם from a תודה. It points out something special about תודה that אשם does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה is brought together with loaves of bread, so it is a 'bigger' offering in some way. Maybe that is why it stays כשר even שלא לשמו. An אשם has no bread, so we cannot assume it works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering
'What about...?': the standard way to point out what makes the source case special, so the comparison fails
Requires bread (the loaves brought with a תודה)

phrases.english: What about a thanks offering?
It is different, because it requires bread!
phrases.notes: The גמרא means the forty loaves that come along with a תודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier attempt (just before this section) to learn אשם from תודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תודה has a special feature (bread) that אשם lacks.

steps.title: Burnt and peace offerings show bread is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: The 'bread' objection is answered: עולה and שלמים have no bread, and they still have the same law.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולה and שלמים will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the bread objection. עולה and שלמים have no bread, yet they are also כשר but not מרצה when slaughtered שלא לשמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bread were the reason, offerings without bread would act differently. Since עולה and שלמים have the same law without any bread, bread cannot be the reason. This sets up the combined argument in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove': another case shows the objection does not hold
Burnt offering
Peace offerings

phrases.english: A burnt offering and a peace offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: Neither of them comes with bread, but they still have this same law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example showing the special feature is not the cause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe תודה's law depends on its bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולה and שלמים have the law without bread, so bread is not the reason.

steps.title: Combined proof from what the offerings share
steps.stepSummary: Each source has its own weakness, so the גמרא builds a הצד השוה argument. The shared feature of all these offerings is that they are קדשים, so אשם, also קדשים, has the same law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument goes back and forth. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that they are holy offerings, and if slaughtered שלא לשמן they are כשר but not מרצה. So I will include אשם too: it is a holy offering, so if slaughtered שלא לשמו it is כשר but not מרצה.
steps.whatsHappening: Each source alone can be knocked down, so the גמרא combines them. It looks only at the feature they all share and applies it to אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולה and שלמים have their own special features, which תודה does not share. תודה has bread, which עולה and שלמים do not have. Since no special feature appears in all of them, the law must come from what they have in common: being קדשים. אשם has that too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reasoning comes back around': each source's weakness is answered by the other
'The look of this one is not like the look of that one': each source is different from the other
The common feature shared by all the sources
Not for their own sake (slaughtered with intent for a different offering)
Does not count for the owner's obligation
Guilt offering

phrases.english: And the reasoning has come back around.
phrases.notes: Each objection to one source is answered by the other source.

phrases.english: This case is not like that case,
and that case is not like this case;
the common feature between them is
that they are holy offerings,
and if one slaughtered them not for their own sake,
it is valid but does not count,
phrases.notes: 'Does not count' means the owner still has not fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: so too I will include a guilt offering,
since it is a holy offering,
and if one slaughtered it not for its own sake,
it is valid but does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין. לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a combined הצד השוה proof out of the sources from the earlier steps.
steps.raayaObject: אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is כשר but אינו מרצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: הצד השוה of תודה, עולה, and שלמים

steps.title: The shared feature is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The הצד השוה argument falls apart. All three source offerings can be brought as a vow or a voluntary gift, but an אשם can only come as a required obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the feature they share? They can all be brought as a נדר or a נדבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the combined proof. It finds a feature that all the sources share and that אשם does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה argument only works if the sources do not share some extra special feature. Here they do: תודה, עולה, and שלמים can all be brought by choice. An אשם is only ever brought because a person must bring it. So maybe being 'voluntary' is the real reason for their law.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow offering ('I take upon myself to bring an offering')
A gift offering (a specific animal set aside by choice)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying אשם is not a holy offering. It agrees אשם is קדשים. The problem is only that the sources share one more feature (being voluntary) that אשם lacks.

phrases.english: What about the common feature between them?
They are special, since they come as a vow or as a gift offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the הצד השוה proof of step 3.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: All the sources share a feature (they can be voluntary) that אשם lacks.

steps.title: רבא's source: the verse links guilt offering to peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the logical arguments and uses a הקש. The פסוק 'זאת התורה' lists אשם next to שלמים, so אשם takes on the law of שלמים: slaughtered שלא לשמו, it is כשר but not מרצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: 'This is the law...' The פסוק puts אשם next to שלמים. Just as שלמים are holy offerings, and if slaughtered שלא לשמן they are כשר but not מרצה, so too I will include אשם, which is a holy offering, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: Since every logic-based proof was knocked down, רבא brings a source straight from a פסוק. The פסוק links אשם with שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A logic-based argument can be broken by finding a difference between the cases. A הקש is a direct link made by the פסוק itself, so differences like bread or being voluntary no longer matter. The word 'אלא' tells us the earlier approaches are being set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': drops the earlier approach and starts a new one
'This is the law': the opening of the פסוק that lists the offerings together
The פסוק compared it (a הֶקֵּשׁ: a link made by placing things together in a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The final source that an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is כשר but does not count for the owner is רבא's הקש. The פסוק 'זאת התורה' places אשם next to שלמים. The logical proofs (from תודה, and from הצד השוה) were all rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a הקש can settle a law when every reasoning-based proof can be picked apart.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
'This is the law, etc.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:37

phrases.english: the verse compared it to peace offerings;
phrases.notes: 'It' is the אשם, which this פסוק lists together with שלמים.

phrases.english: just as peace offerings are holy offerings,
and if one slaughtered them not for their own sake,
they are valid but do not count;
so too I will include a guilt offering,
since it is a holy offering, and so on.
phrases.notes: 'And so on' finishes the same way as before: valid, but does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical proofs fail, it replaces them with a הקש from a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through the הקש to שלמים, an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is כשר but אינו מרצה.

steps.title: Why compare אשם to שלמים and not to חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's הקש: the same פסוק also lists חטאת, so why not compare אשם to חטאת, which becomes פסול when slaughtered שלא לשמה?
steps.simpleTranslation: What made you decide to compare אשם to שלמים? Compare it to חטאת instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the choice made in the last step. The פסוק 'זאת התורה' lists several offerings, so why connect אשם to שלמים in particular?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת slaughtered שלא לשמה is completely פסול. If אשם were compared to חטאת, it would be פסול too, which is the opposite of רבא's ruling. So the challenge is: why choose the lenient comparison over the strict one?

keyTerms.meaning: 'What did you see?' Why did you choose this option over the other one?
Compare through a הֶקֵּשׁ (offerings listed side by side in a פסוק)
Sin offering. It is פסול if slaughtered שלא לשמה

phrases.english: What did you see that you compared it to a peace offering?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the אשם, from רבא's הקש in the last step.

phrases.english: Compare it to a sin offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הקש that רבא used in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice to compare אשם to שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists both חטאת and שלמים next to אשם. Nothing obvious makes שלמים the better match, and a comparison to חטאת would make an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו פסול.

steps.title: The word 'אותה' keeps the חטאת law for חטאת alone
steps.stepSummary: The תורה wrote 'אותה' ('it') about חטאת. This shows that only a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה, so no other offering can be compared to it in this law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תורה excluded other offerings with the word 'אותה' ('it').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק about חטאת says 'אותה', which limits that strict law to the חטאת alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that limits (מיעוט) blocks the comparison to חטאת. Since אשם cannot be compared to חטאת, the only comparison left is to שלמים. That supports רבא's ruling: כשר but not מרצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Excluded or limited, through a word in the פסוק
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה or ה׳
'It', the limiting word in the פסוק about חטאת

steps.whatToRemember: Only a חטאת is פסול when slaughtered שלא לשמה, because of the word 'אותה'. An אשם follows שלמים: it is כשר but does not count for its owner.

phrases.english: But the Merciful One excluded with the word 'it'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:33. 'It' means only the חטאת itself has this strict law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe אשם should be compared to the strict חטאת
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותה' limits the strict law to חטאת, so אשם follows שלמים

steps.title: רב הונא and רב נחמן suggest a reply to ריש לקיש: אשם also comes after death
steps.stepSummary: After a memory-aid, the גמרא tells how רב הונא and רב נחמן, with רב ששת sitting beside them, discussed ריש לקיש's difficulty. ריש לקיש had a problem because אשם is not brought after its owner's death. They suggest רבי אלעזר could have answered that אשם also is brought after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory-aid: ה-נ-ש, ב-ש-ר.) רב הונא and רב נחמן sat, and רב ששת sat with them, and they said: ריש לקיש found it difficult that an אשם is not brought after its owner's death. Let רבי אלעזר answer him: an אשם is also brought after death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory-aid for the names coming up, then starts a new discussion. רב הונא and רב נחמן suggest an answer רבי אלעזר could have given to ריש לקיש's earlier difficulty. רב ששת is sitting with them, and in the next step he answers them (אמר להו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's difficulty assumed that אשם is different from the other offerings because it never comes after the owner dies. רב הונא and רב נחמן challenge that assumption: in some way, an אשם does come after death too. If so, ריש לקיש's difficulty would fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory-aid, letters that help you remember the order of names or topics
Sat. Introduces a scene of rabbis learning together
After death, after the owner of the offering has died
'Let him say to him', suggesting a reply someone could have given

steps.confusionAlert: The text does not yet explain how an אשם 'comes after death'. רב הונא and רב נחמן only say it does, and the details come in the discussion that follows.

phrases.english: (A memory-aid: Heh, Nun, Shin; Beit, Shin, Reish)
phrases.notes: ה-נ-ש stands for הונא, נחמן and ששת, who appear right here. The other letters help you remember the discussion that comes next.

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Nachman were sitting,
and Rav Sheshet was sitting with them,
and they were sitting and saying:
Reish Lakish found it difficult,
about a guilt offering, since it is not brought after death;
let Rabbi Elazar say to him:
A guilt offering is also brought after death!

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב הוּנָא וְרַב נַחְמָן, וְיָתֵיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת גַּבַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that goes back to the earlier argument between ריש לקיש and רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's assumption that אשם is never brought after its owner's death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an אשם can also come after death, then the difference ריש לקיש pointed to does not exist, and רבי אלעזר had an easy reply.

steps.title: רב ששת: only the leftover of an אשם is offered, just like a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rejects the suggested answer. An אשם is not really 'brought after death'. Only its leftover value is used, and a חטאת's leftover is used too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: what part of an אשם is offered after the owner dies? Only its leftover. But a חטאת's leftover is also offered!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת knocks down the idea from the last step that רבי אלעזר could say an אשם is brought after its owner's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the owner dies, the אשם animal itself is never offered. Only the money left over from it is used. A חטאת works the same way, yet a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה. So 'brought after death' cannot be what makes אשם different from חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover: the money from selling the animal, used to buy a different offering
For what is it offered? What part of it is actually offered?

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them:
A guilt offering, in what way is it offered?
phrases.notes: He means: after the owner dies, what part of the אשם actually goes on the מזבח?

phrases.english: Only for its leftover;
phrases.notes: The animal is sold, and the money is used for a different offering.

phrases.english: A sin offering too, its leftover is offered!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אָשָׁם לְמַאי קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer suggested in step 8, that אשם is brought after death.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed answer that 'אשם is brought after death' sets it apart from חטאת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only the leftover of an אשם is offered, and a חטאת's leftover is offered too, so there is no real difference.

steps.title: A חטאת is singled out by the word 'הוא'
steps.stepSummary: The reply to רב ששת: a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה because of a special word in the פסוק, 'הוא', not because of what happens after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חטאת, even though its leftover is offered, the תורה excluded it with the word 'הוא'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת's colleagues answer him. The פסול of a חטאת comes from a special word in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Yes, a חטאת's leftover is also offered, just like an אשם's. But that is not where the חטאת's strict rule comes from. The word 'הוא' ('it is a חטאת') makes a חטאת פסול שלא לשמה, so the leftover point does not cancel the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
The תורה (the Merciful One) excluded it
'It': the extra word in 'it is a חטאת', which teaches that it must be offered for its own sake

phrases.english: A sin offering –
phrases.notes: This is the answer back to רב ששת, from רב הונא and רב נחמן.

phrases.english: even though its leftover is offered,
the Merciful One excluded it with the word "it".
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:24

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטָּאת – אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָרְבָה מוֹתָרַהּ, מִיעֵט רַחֲמָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's rejection by pointing to a פסוק that is unique to חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based distinction: a special word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both offerings have their leftovers offered, they should have the same law.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חטאת's strictness comes from the word 'הוא', so the leftover point does not erase the difference.

steps.title: But the אשם also has the word 'הוא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the word 'הוא' also appears about the אשם, so the אשם should also be פסול שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אשם also has the word 'הוא' written about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. The same special word is written about אשם too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'הוא' is what makes a חטאת פסול when slaughtered for the wrong purpose, then 'הוא ' written about אשם ('it is an אשם') should do the same. That would make אשם just as strict as חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written about it
Guilt offering

phrases.english: A guilt offering too
has "it" written about it!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 10 by finding the same word about אשם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'הוא' sets חטאת apart from אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears about אשם, so by the same reasoning אשם should also be פסול שלא לשמו.

steps.title: The אשם's 'הוא' is about burning the fats, which is not essential
steps.stepSummary: The 'הוא' of אשם is written about the burning of the אימורים. A ברייתא teaches that an אשם is כשר even if the אימורים were never burned, so this 'הוא' cannot make it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: That 'הוא' is written about the stage after the burning of the אימורים, as a ברייתא teaches: about אשם, 'הוא' was said only after the burning of the אימורים, and the אשם itself is כשר even if they did not burn the אימורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word 'הוא' about אשם is not about the main parts of the offering, and it proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אשם, 'הוא' is written next to the burning of the אימורים (the parts burned on the מזבח). That step is not essential: the אשם is כשר even if the אימורים are never burned. A word written about a non-essential stage cannot make the whole אשם פסול, so only חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the offering's fats and parts on the מזבח
As a ברייתא teaches
And it itself, meaning the offering itself
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: Both חטאת and אשם have the word 'הוא', but only for חטאת does it make the offering פסול שלא לשמה. For אשם, the word is about burning the אימורים, which is not essential to the offering.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אשם's 'הוא' means nothing. It is simply about the burning stage, and since the אשם is כשר even with no burning at all, that word cannot make the whole offering פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the strict rule of שלא לשמה stays limited to חטאת, which fits רבא's הקש comparing אשם to שלמים.

phrases.english: That one is about after the burning of the sacrificial portions
that it is written, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
But a guilt offering, "it" was not said about it
except after the burning of the sacrificial portions,
and it itself –
if they did not burn the sacrificial portions, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא לְאַחַר הַקְטָרַת אֵימוּרִים הוּא דִּכְתִיב, כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by limiting the 'הוא' of אשם to the burning of the אימורים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק, supported by a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הוא' written about אשם makes it פסול שלא לשמו, just like חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'הוא' of אשם is about the non-essential burning of the אימורים, so the אשם is not פסול שלא לשמו.

steps.title: What is the word 'It' for, then?
steps.stepSummary: If the 'הוּא' of אשם does not make it פסול שלא לשמו, why does the תורה write it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word 'It'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'הוּא' about the אשם teaches, since we just showed it does not make the אשם פסול. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 removed the obvious job of this word. A word in the תורה is not written for nothing, so the גמרא wants to find its real purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks what a word or rule teaches)
'It', the word in the פסוק about the אשם

phrases.english: But then, why do I need the word 'It'?
phrases.notes: This is the 'הוּא' from step 12, the one written about burning the אימורים of the אשם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 12: once the word is not used to make the אשם פסול, what does it teach?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the word 'הוּא' written about the אשם.

steps.title: The word teaches רב הונא's law about an אשם sent to graze
steps.stepSummary: 'הוּא' is needed for רב הונא's law: an אשם that was ניתק לרעיה and slaughtered without a stated purpose is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what רב הונא said in the name of רב. רב הונא said in the name of רב: an אשם that was sent off to graze, and someone slaughtered it without saying what it was for, is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'הוּא' is the source for a law of רב הונא in the name of רב, about an אשם that was sent out to graze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם that can no longer be brought as an אשם, for example because its owner died, is sent to graze until it gets a blemish. If someone slaughters it before that without stating a purpose, it is כשר as an עולה. The next steps show how 'הוּא' teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent off to graze, meaning officially taken off its job as an אשם
Without saying what purpose it is for
Valid

phrases.english: For what רב הונא said in the name of רב,
for רב הונא said in the name of רב:
An אשם that was sent off to graze,
phrases.notes: This is an אשם that can no longer be brought, so it is put out to pasture until it gets a blemish.

phrases.english: and someone slaughtered it without stating a purpose: it is valid.
phrases.notes: He means it is valid as an עולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הוּא' is the source for רב הונא's law about an אשם that was ניתק לרעיה.

steps.title: Only once it was sent to graze; why?
steps.stepSummary: The law works only if the אשם was ניתק לרעיה. The גמרא asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was sent to graze, yes. If it was not sent to graze, no. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a limit into רב הונא's words, 'that was sent to graze', and asks where that limit comes from. This sets up how the word 'הוּא' teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא made his law depend on the אשם having been ניתק. So before it is ניתק, slaughtering it as an עולה would not work. The question is what keeps it locked as an אשם until then.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
What is the reason?

phrases.english: If it was sent to graze, yes; if it was not sent to graze, no.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיתַּק אִין לֹא נִיתַּק לָא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limit out of רב הונא's law and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an אשם that was not ניתק לרעיה is not כשר when slaughtered without a stated purpose.

steps.title: 'It' means it stays as it is
steps.stepSummary: The word 'הוּא' teaches that the אשם stays an אשם until it is officially sent to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'It': it stays in its status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'הוּא' teaches that the animal keeps its status as an אשם. This is the real job of the word asked about in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הוּא' means 'it is', so it stays an אשם. Only once it is ניתק לרעיה does it leave that status, and only then can it be used as an עולה. This finishes the answer to step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: It stays as it was (in its status)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'הוּא' of אשם does not make it פסול שלא לשמו. It teaches that an אשם stays an אשם until it is ניתק לרעיה (רב הונא's law).

phrases.english: The verse says: 'It',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:5

phrases.english: it shall stay as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and so completes the answer to step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הוּא' teaches that the animal stays an אשם until it is ניתק לרעיה.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש say offerings after death should atone for the heirs?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב ששת ask why ריש לקיש did not reply to רבי אלעזר that offerings brought after death should atone for the heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן and רב ששת were sitting, and רב אדא בר מתנה was sitting with them, and they were saying: about what רבי אלעזר said, 'We have found that offerings brought after the owner's death are כשר but do not atone', ריש לקיש should have answered him: let those also be brought and atone!
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. Three אמוראים look back at the argument between רבי אלעזר and ריש לקיש and ask why ריש לקיש did not push back on one of רבי אלעזר's points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר brought a precedent: offerings brought after the owner died are כשר even though they do not atone. The rabbis ask why ריש לקיש did not answer that these offerings do atone, for the heirs. If so, רבי אלעזר's precedent would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought after the owner's death
Bring atonement (make the owner acceptable before ה')
Let him say to him (why didn't he answer this?)

phrases.english: רב נחמן and רב ששת were sitting,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה גַּבַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and רב אדא בר מתנה was sitting with them,
and they were sitting and saying:
About what רבי אלעזר said,
'We have found, with offerings brought after death,
that they are valid but do not atone',
ריש לקיש should have said to him:
Let those also be brought and atone!
phrases.notes: He means they should atone for the heirs who bring them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about רבי אלעזר's precedent of offerings brought after death.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's precedent that offerings brought after death are כשר but do not atone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If these offerings atone for the heirs, the precedent of a כשר offering that does not atone falls apart, so ריש לקיש should have said so.

steps.title: The heirs have nothing to atone for
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה answers: the offering of a יולדת is for her giving birth. Her children did not give birth, so it cannot atone for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said to them: a woman after childbirth! If she gave birth, did her children give birth?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה explains why ריש לקיש could not make that argument, using the example of a יולדת's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת's offering is brought because she gave birth. If she dies and her heirs bring it, it cannot atone for them, because they never gave birth. So offerings brought after death really are כשר without atoning, and רבי אלעזר's precedent stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth and must bring an offering
Did...? (a question that expects 'no')

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה:
phrases.english: רב אדא בר מתנה said to them:
A woman after childbirth: if she gave birth,
did her children give birth?!
phrases.notes: Her children are her heirs, who bring the offering after she dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה יוֹלֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical answer: the heirs have nothing that needs atonement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offerings brought after death might atone for the heirs, so ריש לקיש could have used that.
steps.terutzMaskana: The offering is tied to the owner's own act, like the יולדת's birth, so it cannot atone for the heirs, and רבי אלעזר's precedent stands.

steps.title: רב אסי: the offering can atone for other sins too, so it can atone for the heirs
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rejects רב אדא בר מתנה's answer. The offering can atone for missed מצוות עשה, so the heirs can also get atonement through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי objects: Who says that if she had several missed positive commandments, she would not get atonement from this offering? Since she does get atonement for them, her heirs also get atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי attacks the answer of רב אדא בר מתנה from Step 18. That answer said the offering is only for giving birth, so it cannot help the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר מתנה said the יולדת's offering is tied only to giving birth. רב אסי points out that her עולה can also atone for her missed מצוות עשה, which have nothing to do with giving birth. So the offering is not locked to birth, and nothing stops it from atoning for her heirs' missed מצוות עשה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects or challenges (introduces an attack on a statement)
A positive commandment (a 'do' מצוה)
She gets atonement
Heirs

phrases.english: Rav Asi objects to this:
And who will tell us
that if she has several positive commandments on her
phrases.notes: He means positive commandments she failed to keep and needs atonement for.

phrases.english: she does not get atonement through it?

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּכִי אִיכָּא כַּמָּה עֲשֵׂה גַּבַּהּ
phrases.english: And since, when she has several positive commandments on her,
she does get atonement,
her heirs also get atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אדא בר מתנה's answer in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר מתנה's claim that the יולדת's offering atones only for giving birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The offering also atones for missed מצוות עשה, so it is not limited to birth, and it can atone for the heirs as well.

steps.title: Do the heirs own the offering? A ruling about a meal offering says no
steps.stepSummary: If the heirs get atonement, that suggests they own the offering. But רבי יוחנן ruled that a מנחה left to two sons is not a partnership, which shows they do not own it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say the heirs own it? But רבי יוחנן said: If someone left a מנחה to his two sons and died, it is offered, and it does not count as a partnership. If you think they own it, the תורה said 'נפש', meaning one person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי's idea. If the offering atones for the heirs, they must own it, but a ruling of רבי יוחנן suggests they do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה cannot be brought by two partners together, because the פסוק says 'נפש', one person. Yet רבי יוחנן says a מנחה left to two sons is offered and is not a partnership offering. That only works if the sons do not own it, and if they do not own it, how can it atone for them?

keyTerms.meaning: It is acquired by them (they own it)
A meal offering made of flour
Partnership, joint ownership
Literally 'a soul'; here it means one single person
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.english: Is this to say that they own it?!
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
If one left a meal offering to his two sons and died,
it is offered, and it does not count as a partnership.
And if you think that they own it,
the Torah said 'a soul'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1. 'Soul' means one person, so a partnership could not bring a meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea in Step 19 that the heirs get atonement through the offering.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the heirs get atonement, which assumes they own the offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Partners cannot bring a מנחה. רבי יוחנן allows a מנחה left to two sons, so the sons must not own it, and it should not atone for them.

steps.title: Do the heirs really not own it? A ruling about swapping an animal says they do
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back the other way. רבי יוחנן also ruled that two sons who inherit an animal offering cannot swap it, and that fits best if they own it as partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they don't own it?! But רבי יוחנן said: If someone left an animal offering to his two sons and died, it is offered, and they cannot make a substitute for it. It makes sense if you say they own it: that is why they cannot make a substitute, because they are like partners,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the conclusion of Step 20 using another ruling of רבי יוחנן. The argument continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an owner who tries to swap his offering animal for another makes the second animal holy too (תמורה). Partners cannot do this. רבי יוחנן says the two sons cannot swap their inherited animal, and the simple reason would be that they own it together as partners. That points back to the heirs owning it, the opposite of Step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a substitute (תְּמוּרָה): trying to swap an offering animal for another one
'It makes sense': introduces a case that fits, before the part that does not fit
That is why
An animal (here, an animal set aside as an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 20 and Step 21 pull in opposite directions. The מנחה ruling suggests the heirs do NOT own the offering. The animal ruling suggests they DO, like partners. The גמרא has to settle this next.

phrases.english: And they don't own it?!
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
If one left an animal offering to his two sons and died,
it is offered, and they cannot make a substitute for it.
It makes sense if you say they own it:
that is why they cannot make a substitute for it,
because they are like partners,
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the other side of 'it makes sense' comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against Step 20's suggestion that the heirs do not own the offering.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 20's suggestion that the heirs do not own the offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Partners cannot make a substitute. רבי יוחנן says the sons cannot make one, which fits best if they own the animal together as partners.
